gaps: Mapuche territorial disputes, dispossession and water-related vulnerability are documented, but their co-occurrence does not establish climate-caused political violence or insecurity interrupting adaptation.
The post-fire protection assessment is a small rapid-interview exercise. Perceived safety and violence concerns do not establish a fire-caused increase or representative prevalence.
A conceptual coastal-water projection without a stated period was excluded rather than assigning a medium-term horizon. Indigenous-disaggregated local exposure information remains incomplete.
The September 2026 water-plan account reports formal measures, pilot indicators and training, not evaluated service improvements or hydrological effects.

executive_assessment.text: Named Mapuche coastal and riverine livelihoods provide local context, alongside historical land and water disputes. Those disputes are not attributed to climate change.
Viña del Mar and Valparaíso fire findings distinguish physical losses, protection needs and response constraints; small-sample perceptions are not prevalence.
National urban/rural water-access differences and the 2026 sector plan identify service and institutional priorities. Basin pilots and training reach are outputs, not measured adaptation effects.
